text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The government has decided to impose tax on agriculture income to meet the demands of the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund, sources said.
- Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto met Sindh provincial Chief Minister Abdullah Shah and reviewed progress in the case of Murtaza Bhutto who was shot dead last month in Karachi.

- The Supreme Court has decided to initiate action against the Chief Election Commissioner for adjourning the hearing of four references pertaining to defections in the provincial assembly of the North West Frontier Province.
- A delegation led by the prime minister's special assistant Shahid Hasan Khan left for Washington to negotiate a new package with the IMF and convince it to resume financial assistance.
- The government is likely to raise the support price of wheat for the 1996/97 crop, sources said.

- A delegation of senior analysts of the U.S.-based credit rating agency Moody's Investors' Service Inc is due in Karachi on October 21 for a week-long visit to meet central bank officials and review Pakistan's investment and credit rating.
- A delegation of the European Union is coming to Pakistan in February 1997 to investigate dumping charges against 23 bedwear manufacturers and exports.
- Petrofac of Britain and Titan/Sembawang of Canada have been short-listed for a $50 million contract to build a gas purification plant.
- The government has decided to abolish a 10 percent regulatory duty on imports, sources said.

- A meeting of opposition parties strongly criticised the government's decision to fully submit to the IMF's demands and said imposition of new taxes without approval of the National Assembly (lower house) would be illegal.
- As many as 127 textile mills out of a total of 503 have been closed down for various reasons, the Textile Commissioner informed the Finance Ministry.
